project: Namias Portfolio - Blog Section on Home (2-column with Certifications)
summary: Surface the existing /blog content as a compact Blog section on the home page, rendered in a 2-column layout side-by-side with the Certifications section. Reuses the existing BlogPost data, the IS_BLOG_VISIBLE feature flag, and the established Card + framer-motion patterns. The /blog route and the Sanity-driven data pipeline are not modified.
narrative: The portfolio already has a full /blog route, a BlogPost type, Sanity-backed blogPosts in the CMS payload, fallback content, an ISR-cached [slug] route, sitemap entries, and a feature flag (IS_BLOG_VISIBLE=false) that currently 404s the route. Despite that, the home page never surfaces any blog content. Hiring managers and visitors who land on / never see a signal that the owner writes. This PRD introduces a compact BlogSection card on the home page that shows the latest 3 posts (cover thumb, title, date · readTime, excerpt, tags) and a 'View all' link to /blog. The section is rendered in a new 2-column grid (Blog on the left, Certifications on the right) below the existing main two-column layout, with a single-column stack on mobile. The change is additive: no existing section is removed, /blog is unchanged, and the feature flag continues to gate the whole experience so the build remains safe in production until explicitly enabled.
principles: Reuse what exists - no new data types, no new fetcher, no new route. Only a new consumer component and one layout change.
Feature-flagged - the entire feature is hidden when IS_BLOG_VISIBLE=false, matching the rest of the codebase.
Compact and quiet - the section complements, not competes with, Certifications. 3 posts maximum on the home card.
Type-safe and tested - tsc, eslint, vitest, and react-doctor must all stay green.
One story slice per commit - planning, flag flip, component, layout, tests, docs are separate commits.
No comments in code - the only documentation is the PRD, the section header text, and any JSDoc the type demands.

designDecisions.choice: A new grid row below the existing 2-column main layout. On >= lg it is grid-cols-2; on < lg it stacks (Blog on top, Certifications below).
designDecisions.rationale: Preserves the existing main 2-column structure (About/Tech/Projects vs Experience/Connect) and only changes the lower row. Keeps the sticky balance logic untouched.

designDecisions.choice: Both cards stretch to the height of the taller one (default grid items behavior, no manual height set).
designDecisions.rationale: Certifications is the dense block (filter tabs + 2-col grid). Blog is a short list of 3. Letting grid stretch is enough; no JS needed.

designDecisions.choice: Show latest 3 posts by date desc, with cover thumb (Next/Image, 80x80 or 96x96), title, date + readTime, 2-line excerpt, and up to 2 tag chips.
designDecisions.rationale: 3 posts fits comfortably in a half-width card on desktop. Excerpt length matches the line-clamp pattern used by ProjectsSection and RecommendationsCarousel.

designDecisions.choice: If blogPosts is empty and IS_BLOG_VISIBLE=true, render a single friendly card with a 'No posts yet' message and a link to /blog. No skeleton loader.
designDecisions.rationale: Empty state is the steady state for the demo. Skeletons are reserved for slow SWR fetches that this card does not do.

designDecisions.choice: Gate at three levels: (a) the route /blog still 404s when IS_BLOG_VISIBLE=false, (b) the Hero Blog link is hidden, (c) the new home BlogSection returns null when IS_BLOG_VISIBLE=false. The flag flips to true in its own commit at the end.
designDecisions.rationale: Defence in depth. The owner can ship code with the flag off and flip it on after visual review, matching the existing pattern in src/lib/features.ts.

designDecisions.choice: Cover the BlogSection in isolation (renders N posts, empty state, flag-off returns null) and add a smoke test in app-layout-page.test.tsx that the home page renders the section when the flag is on.
designDecisions.rationale: Matches the pattern in src/__tests__/components/sections-uncovered.test.tsx for CertificationsSection.

epics.title: Plan & data audit
epics.summary: Write the PRD, audit the existing blog data shape and the home page layout, and confirm no schema changes are needed.

stories.title: Write PRD for the home blog section
stories.details: Author prd.blog.json with epics, stories, success metrics, non-goals, and design decisions. Place at the repo root next to prd.json.

stories.title: Audit blogPost shape and CMS pipeline
stories.details: Read src/types/index.ts (BlogPost), src/lib/cms-content.shared.ts (fallbackBlogPosts), src/lib/cms-content.server.ts (server fetcher), and src/hooks/useCmsContent.ts (client hook). Confirm blogPosts is already in the payload and a consumer just needs useCmsContent().blogPosts.

stories.title: Audit home page layout breakpoints
stories.details: Read src/app/page.tsx and confirm the existing grid is lg:grid-cols-[62%_1fr] with a 1-col mobile fallback. Plan a new full-width row below Certifications that becomes 2-col at lg.

epics.title: BlogSection component
epics.summary: Create src/components/sections/BlogSection.tsx as a client component that reads useCmsContent().blogPosts, sorts by date desc, and renders the latest 3 posts as a vertical list with a header and a 'View all' link.

stories.title: Create BlogSection skeleton with feature flag gate
stories.details: Create src/components/sections/BlogSection.tsx. Import IS_BLOG_VISIBLE and useCmsContent. Return null when the flag is off. Render a <section> with a header (h2 'Blog', count badge) and a 'View all' link to /blog when the flag is on.

stories.title: Render latest 3 posts as a vertical list
stories.details: Sort blogPosts by date desc, take 3, and map to a list item with: cover (next/image, 80x80, lazy), title (link to /blog/<slug>), meta (date + readTime, e.g. 'May 12, 2026 - 5 min read'), 2-line clamped excerpt, and up to 2 tag chips. Use the existing Card primitives and framer-motion entry animations like the rest of the sections.

stories.title: Add empty state for when no posts exist
stories.details: When blogPosts.length === 0 (and flag is on), render a small empty-state card: 'No posts yet' with a 'Visit the blog' link. No skeleton.

stories.title: Add resolveContentImageSrc + Image alt text
stories.details: Use resolveContentImageSrc (from src/lib/media) to resolve cover images consistently with CertificationsSection. Always set a non-empty alt from the post title.

epics.title: Home page layout integration
epics.summary: Add a new full-width row below the existing 2-column main grid that becomes a 2-column grid (Blog | Certifications) at lg breakpoint and stacks on smaller screens.

stories.title: Wrap Certifications + BlogSection in a 2-col grid
stories.details: In src/app/page.tsx, replace the single Certifications Card with a new <div className='mt-4 grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2 gap-4'> containing <Card><BlogSection /></Card> and <Card><CertificationsSection /></Card>. Keep the Gallery Card and Footer below as-is.

stories.title: Preserve sticky balance for the main grid above
stories.details: The new Blog+Cert row sits below the existing 2-column grid. Do not touch leftColumnRef / rightColumnRef / stickySide logic.

epics.title: Tests
epics.summary: Add component-level tests for BlogSection and a smoke test in the home page layout test confirming the section renders when the flag is on and is absent when the flag is off.

stories.title: Add BlogSection component tests
stories.details: Add src/__tests__/components/sections/BlogSection.test.tsx. Cover: (a) returns null when IS_BLOG_VISIBLE=false, (b) renders 3 latest posts when IS_BLOG_VISIBLE=true, (c) renders empty state when blogPosts is empty, (d) link to /blog and per-post links use the correct href. Mock useCmsContent and IS_BLOG_VISIBLE per test.

stories.title: Extend app-layout-page test for the new row
stories.details: Update src/__tests__/app/app-layout-page.test.tsx. Add a mock for @/components/sections/BlogSection. Assert the mock renders inside the new 2-col row when the flag is on, and does not render when the flag is off (use vi.mock of @/lib/features).

epics.title: Flag flip & docs
epics.summary: Flip IS_BLOG_VISIBLE to true once the component, layout, and tests are merged, and add a short note in AGENTS.md.

stories.title: Flip IS_BLOG_VISIBLE to true
stories.details: Set IS_BLOG_VISIBLE = true in src/lib/features.ts. Verify / no longer 404s on /blog link, and the home card renders.

stories.title: Document the section in AGENTS.md
stories.details: Add a one-line entry under 'Skills' or a new 'Sections' subsection noting the BlogSection component path and its feature flag.

epics.title: Verification
epics.summary: Run the full quality gate: typecheck, lint, vitest, react-doctor, dev server smoke test.

stories.title: Run tsc, eslint, vitest
stories.details: Run: npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, npm run test -- --run. All must pass with the new tests included.

stories.title: Run react-doctor
stories.details: Run npm run doctor. Score must stay at 100/100. If a finding lands, fix it in the same PR following the fix-react-doctor-finding skill.

stories.title: Dev server smoke test
stories.details: Curl http://localhost:3000/ and confirm the SSR HTML contains the Blog section header and the 3 post titles. Curl http://localhost:3000/blog and confirm the route resolves. Take a screenshot if a browser tool is available.

openQuestions: Should the BlogSection show post cover images, or a text-only list? The PRD currently plans a small 80x80 cover, matching the visual weight of the certification cards.
Should the 'View all' link open in the same tab or a new tab? The PRD plans same-tab (Link component) to match the rest of the home page.

If blogPosts has more than 3 entries, should the section show a 'See all 12' count in the header, or just a 'View all ->' link? The PRD plans a count badge in the header and a 'View all' link below the list.
Should the section support a tag filter like Certifications supports an issuer filter? The PRD plans no filter (compact list of 3), but it can be added in a follow-up if needed.
